elements.quote: second interim results of a living systematic review

elements.quote: The Delta variant has become the dominant strain of SARS-CoV-2. We summarised the evidence on COVID19 vaccine effectiveness (VE) identified in 17 studies that investigated VE against different endpoints. ... The Delta variant (Phylogenetic Assignment of Named Global Outbreak (Pango) lineage designation B.1.617.2) of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) was first reported in October 2020 and has spread to more than 180 countries globally [1]. Concerns were raised about how well the currently available vaccines protect against this variant.
elements.reason: The text describes the current state of knowledge (Delta variant spread) and important uncertainties (concerns about vaccine protection).

elements.quote: Concerns were raised about how well the currently available vaccines protect against this variant. Since January 2021, the Robert Koch Institute (RKI), in collaboration with the National Immunisation Technical Advisory Groups (NITAGs) network coordinated by the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) is performing a living systematic review on the efficacy, effectiveness and safety of coronavirus disease (COVID-19) vaccines authorised in the European Union (EU) (PROSPERO registration: CRD42020208935) [2]. Here we present results on the effectiveness and the duration of protection provided by the EU-licensed COVID-19 vaccines in respect to the Delta variant.
elements.reason: The text explains the importance and need for the review by highlighting concerns about vaccine protection against the dominant variant and stating the purpose of the living systematic review.

elements.quote: Since January 2021, the Robert Koch Institute (RKI), in collaboration with the National Immunisation Technical Advisory Groups (NITAGs) network coordinated by the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) is performing a living systematic review on the efficacy, effectiveness and safety of coronavirus disease (COVID-19) vaccines authorised in the European Union (EU) (PROSPERO registration: CRD42020208935) [2].
